title: 第十八章 薪传
content_zh:
炉中药膳的香气，在接下来的数日里，成了医舍里除却惯常药味之外，最为恒定的气息。

    石耳、赤精枣、黄芪，这三样并非什么珍稀灵药，甚至大多时候只被视作稍有补益的凡俗之物。但在苏芸的指点下，陈默严格把控着火候、水量、煎煮时间，甚至加入药膳的次序。他不再像服用铁骨草汁时那样莽撞，而是将这次药膳的熬煮，也当作一种“修炼”——专注，耐心，观察着每一次气泡的翻腾，每一缕蒸汽的升腾，感受着不同药材在沸水中缓慢释放药性的细微变化。

    药膳的味道谈不上好，石耳的菌香里混着黄芪淡淡的土腥和赤精枣过于温吞的甜，入喉后，一股温吞吞的暖意自胃部升起，不似血筋膏那般有力，也不似断续藤那般苦涩霸道，却胜在连绵不绝，如同春日的微雨，悄无声息地浸润着干涸龟裂的土地。配合着苏芸所授的那套呼吸法，这药力化开得似乎更为匀净，丝丝缕缕，渗入受伤的筋骨经脉，也沉淀进亏损的气血之中。

    陈默每日晨昏，雷打不动地练习那套呼吸法。最初依旧滞涩，心神难以完全契合那种与周围环境隐隐共鸣的韵律，但随着时间的推移，以及药膳和自身伤势缓慢好转带来的正向反馈，他渐渐摸到了一点门道。不再强求与苏芸演示的完全一致，而是寻找着自身气息、伤势状况与外界环境之间，那个最为平衡舒适的“点”。有时是倚在门边，对着小院里那几丛夜交藤；有时是坐在床沿，听着窗外渐沥的雨声或远处的虫鸣。一呼一吸，悠长而平稳，意念放得极轻，仿佛只是旁观着气息在体内的自然流转，与外界气息的无声交汇。

    效果并非立竿见影。左肩的隐痛依旧在特定动作时清晰传来，胸口那堵“墙”也依然厚重。但他能感觉到，一些更深层的东西在缓慢改变。比如，睡眠变得沉实了些，梦魇般的厮杀场景和坠落的失重感不再频繁侵扰；比如，运行《引气诀》时，心神更容易沉静，杂念丛生的时间在减少；又比如，左臂虽然依旧无力，但那种仿佛与身体其他部分脱节、冰冷麻木的感觉，似乎在减轻，指尖重新有了些微弱的、属于自己的温度。

    苏芸所授的呼吸法，与《引气诀》并非替代关系，更像是一种补充和调和。吐纳重在引气、炼气、行气，目标明确，却也容易因执着和瓶颈而产生焦躁滞涩。而这呼吸法，则弱化了“目的”，更侧重于“过程”本身，在于“养”与“和”，让身体在一种更为自然放松的状态下，接受灵气的温养，也潜移默化地修复着自身的损伤与失衡。陈默开始尝试在吐纳前后，加入一段时间的呼吸法练习，作为预热与收尾，感觉确实顺畅不少。

    他开始重新翻阅那本周安笔记。这一次，带着苏芸传授的、更为系统清晰的草药知识，以及那份对“知其然更需知其所以然”的认知。果然，他发现笔记中许多语焉不详、甚至看似矛盾的地方，在苏芸的点拨下，豁然开朗。那些粗陋的炮制方法，背后或许隐藏着资源极度匮乏下的无奈妥协；那些模糊的药性描述，也因明确了生长环境、采摘时令、配伍禁忌，而变得立体可信。他不再全盘接受，也不再轻易否定，而是学会了带着审慎和思考去阅读，尝试理解周安执事当年记录这些文字时，所处的境地与局限。

    他甚至拿出之前收集的铁骨草和青礞石，对照笔记和苏芸的讲解，重新审视。铁骨草需配伍柔筋花、甘泉水，去燥存效；青礞石需反复淘洗沉淀，取其精华去其糟粕……这些，笔记上或未提及，或一笔带过，而苏芸却给出了具体可行的方法。陈默心中恍然，又有些后怕。若无苏芸指点，他恐怕会在这条“自行摸索”的路上，走更多弯路，甚至踏入歧途。

    他将这些新的认知，用炭笔仔细记录在日课纸的背面，与往日的修炼心得、体悟混杂在一起。字迹依旧工整，但内容已不再仅限于枯燥的“气感运行几何息”，开始出现“墨叶兰，喜阴湿，溪畔石缝，三年紫根方可用”，“石耳，清肺热，缓火毒，需配黄芪调和”，“呼吸法贵在自然，强求反失其韵”等等更为丰富具体的记载。这张纸，正从一个简单的修炼日志，演变成他独有的、融合了修炼、疗伤、草药认知乃至生存体悟的杂记。

    五日后，晨光微露，陈默再次准时出现在杂役院后门的木栅栏旁。

    苏芸已等在那里，依旧是那副清淡如水的模样。看到他，目光在他脸上停留了一瞬，几不可察地点了点头，似乎对他气色的些微改善表示认可，但并未多言，只是转身，再次没入山林。

    这一次，她带陈默走的是一条略有不同的路径，更偏东北方向。林木更加高大，树冠几乎遮蔽了天空，林下光线幽暗，地面铺着厚厚的、不知积累了多少年的腐殖质，踩上去柔软而富有弹性，散发出一股浓郁的、带着甜腥气的腐朽与新生交织的味道。空气更加湿润，灵气浓度似乎也比上次那溪边空地更高了些，呼吸间都能感到一丝微凉的、润泽的意味。

    “今日带你认几种对稳固心神、辅助突破小瓶颈略有裨益的草药。”苏芸在一处生着许多蕨类植物和苔藓的湿润坡地前停下，声音在寂静的林间显得格外清晰，“但此类草药，往往伴生着迷惑心神或略有毒性的植物，需仔细辨别。”

    她指着一丛叶片细长如针、呈墨绿色、顶端开着米粒大小白色小花的植物：“这是‘定魂草’，取其根部，晾干研磨，点燃后的烟气，有微弱安定神魂、抵御低阶幻术侵扰之效。是炼制‘静心符’和某些宁神丹药的辅料。”她又指向旁边一株外形略似、但叶片稍宽、顶端开着淡紫色小花的植物，“这是‘乱神花’，与定魂草伴生，外形极为相似，唯花色与叶形略有差异。其花粉有致幻之能，误服或吸入过多，可令人心神恍惚，产生幻觉。采摘时，需万分小心，最好以湿布掩住口鼻。”

    陈默凑近，凝神细看。果然，两者叶片纹理、花朵形态、甚至散发出的极其淡薄的气味，都有细微差别。若不仔细辨别，极易混淆。他将这些差异牢牢记在心里，甚至蹲下身，用手指轻轻触碰两种植物的叶片，感受其质地，又凑近闻了闻（小心避开了乱神花的花朵）。定魂草的叶片更硬挺，带着一丝清凉的草木气；乱神花的叶片稍软，气味更淡，几乎难以察觉。

    “修仙之路，诱惑与危险并存。有时，机缘与陷阱，只在一线之间。”苏芸的声音在头顶响起，平静无波，“识药如此，识人、识事、乃至识这天地大道，亦是如此。眼要明，心要细，不可全信，亦不可不信。需有自己的判断。”

    陈默默然点头，将这话记在心里。他知道，苏芸所指，绝非仅仅是眼前这两株草药。

    接着，苏芸又带他辨认了附近另外几种草药：一种名为“凝露果”的红色小浆果，生长在背阴的岩石上，受夜露滋养，蕴含极微薄的纯净水灵气，直接服食可润泽干涸的经脉，对火毒或修炼燥热功法导致的经脉灼伤有缓解之效，但不可多食，性凉。一种攀附在老树上的、开淡黄色铃铛状小花的“木铃兰”，取其花朵阴干，香气有安神助眠之效，可缝制香囊佩戴，或置于枕边。还有一种长在腐木上的、伞盖呈灰白色、有同心圆纹路的“地灵芝”，并非灵药，但常年受此地灵气滋养，有微弱补中益气、强健脾胃之效，可作药膳。

    每认一种，苏芸不仅讲解其形态、药性、用法，更会提及可能的伴生毒物、采摘处理注意事项，以及一些简单的、适合陈默现在条件（无丹炉、无复杂工具）的炮制或使用方法。她的知识体系显然远比周安笔记系统完整，且更为实用。

    辨认完草药，苏芸并未立刻返回，而是带着陈默继续向山林深处走了一段。周围的灵气越发浓郁，光线也更加幽暗，仿佛进入了另一个世界。参天古木的根系如虬龙般裸露在地表，上面覆盖着厚厚的、色彩斑斓的苔藓。不知名的藤蔓从树冠垂落，开着奇异的花朵。空气中弥漫着一股淡淡的、类似檀香又混合着腐朽气息的奇异味道。

    “此处已深入灵雾区边缘，灵气较杂，驳而不纯，且偶有低阶妖虫出没，不可久留。”苏芸在一处较为干燥、背靠巨大岩壁的空地停下，转身看向陈默，“但此地木灵之气与水土之气交汇，对你温养木、水两系灵根，稳固心神，略有裨益。你且在此，运转我传你的呼吸法一炷香时间，感受与在杂役院中有何不同。”

    陈默依言，走到岩壁下一块较为平坦的青石上盘膝坐下，闭上眼，开始运转那套呼吸法。一进入状态，他立刻感觉到了明显的不同。

    杂役院中，灵气稀薄驳杂，运行呼吸法时，更多是调理自身气息，与外界共鸣微弱。而在此地，即便只是边缘，灵气浓度也高出数倍。随着他呼吸节奏的调整，周遭那湿润的、带着草木与泥土芬芳的灵气，仿佛受到了无形的吸引，开始缓缓向他周身汇聚。虽然依旧微弱，但比起在杂役院时几乎无法感知的情形，已是天壤之别。

    更重要的是，此地的灵气属性似乎更为明显。他能隐约感觉到，那随着呼吸渗入体内的灵气中，有一股清凉润泽的意味（水？），和一股生机勃勃、却又带着些许腐朽沉淀气息的意味（木？土？）。这两种属性的灵气，随着呼吸法的引导，缓缓融入他体内那缕无属性的暖流之中，虽然数量极少，几乎可以忽略不计，却让他那因伤势和长期灵气匮乏而显得干涩滞涩的经脉，感受到了一丝久旱逢甘霖般的滋润和舒缓。胸口那堵“墙”似乎也在这润泽下，变得不那么“燥硬”。

    一炷香时间很快过去。陈默缓缓睁开眼睛，长舒一口气。只觉神清气爽，多日来因伤病和琐事带来的沉郁疲惫之感一扫而空，体内暖流似乎也活泼凝实了一分。虽然距离突破瓶颈还遥遥无期，但这种清晰感受到进步、身体与周遭环境和谐共鸣的感觉，实在令人着迷。
content_en:
In the next few days, the aroma of the medicinal food in the furnace became the most constant smell in the hospital besides the usual medicinal smell.
Stone fungus, red jujube, and astragalus are not rare elixirs, and most of the time they are only regarded as mundane things with mild benefits.But under Su Yun's guidance, Chen Mo strictly controlled the heat, amount of water, cooking time, and even the order of adding medicinal foods.He was no longer as reckless as when he took the iron bone grass juice, but regarded the cooking of this medicinal meal as a kind of "practice" - focusing and being patient, observing every bubble rolling, every wisp of steam rising, and feeling the subtle changes in the slow release of medicinal properties of different medicinal materials in boiling water.
The taste of the medicinal food cannot be said to be good. The fungus aroma of Shi fungus is mixed with the faint earthiness of astragalus and the overly sweetness of red dates. After entering the throat, a warm feeling rises from the stomach. It is not as powerful as the blood tendon ointment, nor as bitter and overbearing as the scimitar vine, but it is better than the continuous one, like the light rain in spring, quietly infiltrating the dry and cracked land.In conjunction with the breathing technique taught by Su Yun, the medicinal power seemed to be spread more evenly, seeping into the injured muscles and meridians, and also settling into the depleted Qi and blood.
Chen Mo practiced that breathing method every morning and evening.At first he was still stagnant, and it was difficult for his mind to fully conform to the rhythm that vaguely resonated with the surrounding environment. But as time went by, and with the positive feedback brought by the medicinal diet and the slow improvement of his own injuries, he gradually gained some knowledge.No longer insisting on being exactly the same as what Su Yun demonstrated, but looking for the most balanced and comfortable "point" between one's own aura, injury status and the external environment.Sometimes I lean against the door, facing the clumps of night vines in the courtyard; sometimes I sit on the edge of the bed, listening to the sound of rain falling outside the window or the chirping of insects in the distance.Breathing in and out, long and steady, with very light thoughts, as if just watching the natural flow of breath in the body and the silent interaction with the outside breath.
The effects are not immediate.The dull pain in my left shoulder still came clearly during certain movements, and the "wall" in my chest was still thick.But he could feel that something deeper was slowly changing.For example, sleep has become heavier, and nightmare-like fighting scenes and the weightless feeling of falling are no longer frequently intrusive; for example, when running "Qi Entrainment Technique", the mind is easier to calm down, and the time for distracting thoughts is reduced; for another example, although the left arm is still weak, the cold and numb feeling that seems to be disconnected from the rest of the body seems to be lessening, and the fingertips have a faint, own temperature again.
The breathing method taught by Su Yun is not a substitute for the "Qi-Yining Jue", but more like a complement and reconciliation.Breathing and breathing focus on entraining, refining, and moving Qi. The goal is clear, but it is also easy to cause anxiety and stagnation due to persistence and bottlenecks.This breathing method weakens the "purpose" and focuses more on the "process" itself, on "nourishing" and "harmony", allowing the body to accept the warmth and nourishment of spiritual energy in a more natural and relaxed state, and also subtly repair its own damage and imbalance.Chen Mo began to try to add a period of breathing exercises before and after exhaling as a warm-up and finish, and it felt much smoother indeed.
He began to look through his notes for the week again.This time, with the more systematic and clear knowledge of herbal medicine taught by Su Yun, as well as the understanding that "to know what is happening, we need to know why."Sure enough, he found many unclear and even seemingly contradictory places in his notes. With Su Yun's guidance, they suddenly became clear.Behind those crude preparation methods, there may be helpless compromises due to extreme scarcity of resources; those vague descriptions of medicinal properties have also become three-dimensional and credible because the growing environment, picking season, and compatibility taboos are clarified.He no longer accepted it all, nor did he deny it easily. Instead, he learned to read with caution and thinking, trying to understand the situation and limitations that Deacon Zhou An was in when he recorded these words.
He even took out the Iron Bone Grass and Qingzhen Stone that he had collected before, and reviewed them again by comparing his notes with Su Yun's explanation.Iron bone grass needs to be mixed with soft tendon flowers and sweet spring water to remove dryness and retain the effect; Qingzhen stone needs to be washed and precipitated repeatedly to extract the essence and remove the dross... These are either not mentioned in the notes, or are briefly mentioned, but Su Yun gave specific and feasible methods.Chen Mo suddenly felt enlightened and a little scared.Without Su Yun's guidance, he might have taken more detours or even gone astray on this "self-exploration" road.
He carefully recorded these new understandings on the back of the daily lesson paper with charcoal, and mixed them with his past cultivation experiences and insights.The handwriting is still neat and tidy, but the content is no longer limited to the boring "geometric movement of Qi". More rich and specific records have begun to appear, such as "Black leaf orchid, likes dampness and dampness, and can be used in the cracks of rocks beside the stream. Purple roots can only be used after three years."This piece of paper is evolving from a simple training diary into his unique miscellany that combines training, healing, knowledge of herbal medicines, and even survival experiences.
Five days later, in the morning light, Chen Mo appeared on time again at the wooden fence at the back door of the courtyard.
Su Yun was waiting there, still looking as calm as water.Seeing him, her eyes stayed on his face for a moment, and she nodded almost imperceptibly, seeming to acknowledge the slight improvement in his complexion, but without saying anything more, she just turned around and disappeared into the forest again.
This time, she took Chen Mo along a slightly different path, more northeastward.The forest trees are taller, and the canopy almost blocks the sky. The light under the forest is dim, and the ground is covered with thick humus that has accumulated for countless years. It is soft and elastic when stepped on, and exudes a rich, sweet smell of decay and new life.The air is more humid, and the concentration of spiritual energy seems to be higher than that in the open space by the stream last time. You can feel a slight coolness and moistness in your breath.
"Today I will introduce you to several herbs that are slightly helpful in stabilizing the mind and helping to break through small bottlenecks." Su Yun stopped in front of a moist slope with many ferns and mosses. Her voice was particularly clear in the silent forest. "But such herbs are often accompanied by plants that confuse the mind or are slightly toxic, so they need to be carefully identified."
She pointed to a clump of plants with needle-like leaves, dark green leaves and small white flowers the size of rice grains on the top: "This is the 'soul-fixing grass'. Take the root, dry it and grind it. The smoke after lighting has the effect of weakly calming the soul and resisting the intrusion of low-level illusions. It is an auxiliary material for refining the 'quiet mind' and some tranquilizing elixirs." She pointed to a plant next to it.It is a plant with a slightly similar shape, but with slightly wider leaves and small lavender flowers on the top. "This is the 'Lost Flower', which is associated with the Soul-Dinging Grass. The appearance is very similar, but the flower color and leaf shape are slightly different. Its pollen has hallucinogenic properties. If swallowed or inhaled too much, it can make people feel trance-like and hallucinate. When picking, you need to be extremely careful, and it is best to cover your mouth and nose with a wet cloth."
Chen Mo came closer and took a closer look.Sure enough, there are subtle differences in the texture of the leaves, the shape of the flowers, and even the extremely light smell emitted by the two.If you don't distinguish carefully, it can be easily confused.He kept these differences in mind, and even crouched down and gently touched the leaves of the two plants with his fingers to feel their texture, and then smelled them closer (carefully avoiding the flowers of the Luan Shenhua).The leaves of Dinghuncao are stiffer and have a cool grassy smell; the leaves of Luanshenhua are slightly softer and the smell is lighter and almost imperceptible.
"On the road to cultivating immortality, temptations and dangers coexist. Sometimes, opportunities and traps are just a thin line apart." Su Yun's voice sounded above her head, calm and waveless, "It's the same with knowing medicine, knowing people, knowing things, and even knowing the avenue of heaven and earth. The eyes must be clear, the heart must be careful, you can't believe everything, and you can't not believe it. You need to make your own judgment."
Chen Moran nodded and kept these words in mind.He knew that Su Yun was not just referring to the two herbs in front of him.
Then, Su Yun led him to identify several other nearby herbs: a small red berry called "Gel Condensation Fruit", which grows on shady rocks and is nourished by night dew. It contains a very small amount of pure water spiritual energy. Taking it directly can moisturize dry meridians. It has an effect on relieving meridians burns caused by fire poison or practicing dry-heat techniques. However, do not eat too much as it is cool in nature.A kind of "wooden bell lily" with small pale yellow bell-shaped flowers clinging to old trees. Its flowers are dried in the shade. Its aroma has the effect of soothing the mind and promoting sleep. It can be sewn into a sachet and worn, or placed on the pillow.There is also a kind of "Lingzhi" that grows on rotten wood, has a gray-white canopy and has concentric circles. It is not a panacea, but it is nourished by the spiritual energy of this place all year round. It has the effect of weakly replenishing Qi and strengthening the spleen and stomach, and can be used as a medicinal diet.
For each item, Su Yun not only explained its form, medicinal properties, and usage, but also mentioned possible associated poisons, precautions for picking and handling, as well as some simple preparation or use methods suitable for Chen Mo's current conditions (no pill furnace, no complicated tools).Her knowledge system is obviously far more complete and more practical than Zhou An's note-taking system.
After identifying the herbs, Su Yun did not return immediately, but continued walking deeper into the forest with Chen Mo.The aura around him became thicker and the light became darker, as if he had entered another world.The roots of towering ancient trees are exposed on the surface like horned dragons, covered with thick, colorful moss.Unknown vines hang down from the tree crown, bearing strange flowers.The air was filled with a faint, strange smell that was similar to sandalwood mixed with the smell of decay.
"This place has gone deep into the edge of the spiritual mist area. The spiritual energy is mixed and impure, and low-level demonic insects occasionally appear. Don't stay here for a long time." Su Yun stopped in a relatively dry open space with a huge rock wall at her back, and turned to look at Chen Mo, "ButThe aura of the wood spirit and the aura of water and earth intersect here, which is slightly beneficial to your spiritual roots of wood and water, and to stabilize your mind.If you are here and perform the breathing method I teach you for one stick of incense, you will feel it is different from that in the courtyard."
